mainTopic: A husband's expenses on and benefit from his wife's property: what counts as 'eating', repayment rules, sharecroppers, and selling the produce
overview: The גמרא continues the משנה's rule about a husband who spends money on his wife's property. If he 'ate' even a little from it, he cannot claim his expenses back. It defines how little counts: even a cluster of dates. Date dough is a תיקו. If he did not eat in a dignified way, two אמוראים disagree whether it takes an איסר's worth or a דינר's worth. רב יהודה ruled that using vine branches also counts, which fits his view on חזקה. רב חסדא rules that a husband of a קטנה is repaid like an outsider, so that he will take care of her property. A story with רבי אמי teaches that taking from the principal is not 'eating', so the husband swears and collects. רבי אסי, explained by אביי and then רבא, limits what he collects to the value of the improvement, and only with an oath. Finally the גמרא asks whether sharecroppers the husband hired leave when he leaves; רב הונא בריה דרב יהושע says it depends on whether the husband could farm himself. The amud ends by starting a new question: whether a husband may sell the produce of his wife's land.

steps.title: Even a cluster of dates counts as eating
steps.stepSummary: In the name of רבי אבא, the house of רב rules that even a cluster of dates counts as 'eating' from the wife's property.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אבא reports that the house of רב says: even a cluster of dates is enough.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is finishing a list of opinions about the smallest amount of produce a husband must eat to count as having 'eaten' from his wife's property. The house of רב says that even a stuck-together cluster of dates counts.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה says that if the husband ate even a little, he cannot claim his expenses. This opinion sets a very low bar, since a clump of dates is a small, simple food. The point is that what matters is that he truly ate in a normal, dignified way, not the amount.

keyTerms.meaning: A cluster or clump of dates stuck together
The house of study of רב

steps.confusionAlert: This line continues a סוגיא that started on the previous page. The words 'even a cluster of dates' answer the question 'how much counts as eating a little?'

phrases.english: Rabbi Abba: they say in the house of Rav:
Even a cluster of dates.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the definition of the minimum amount of 'eating' begun on the previous page.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Even eating a cluster of dates from the wife's property counts as eating, so the husband loses his claim for expenses.

steps.title: What about dough made of dates?
steps.stepSummary: רב ביבי asks whether eating dough made from dates also counts as eating.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב ביבי asked: what is the law for date dough?
steps.whatsHappening: רב ביבי asks a follow-up question about a different date food: dates mashed into a dough.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A cluster of dates is eaten in a normal way. Date dough is less clearly a dignified way of eating, so it is unclear whether it is considered real eating. The question tests where the line of 'proper eating' lies.

keyTerms.meaning: He asked (a real question of law)
Dough or paste made of dates

phrases.english: Rav Beivai asked:
Date dough, what is the law?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Extends the cluster-of-dates ruling to a borderline case.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether eating date dough from the wife's property counts as dignified eating that cancels the husband's claim.

steps.title: The question stays unresolved
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא leaves רב ביבי's question as a תיקו.
steps.simpleTranslation: Let it stand unresolved.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא ends רב ביבי's question without an answer. It is a תיקו.
steps.deeperAnalysis: No source decides whether date dough counts as eating. So the question about date dough remains open.

keyTerms.meaning: Let it stand: the question remains unresolved

phrases.english: Let it stand.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Closes the question of step 2 without a resolution.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: Whether date dough counts as eating is left undecided.

steps.title: What if he did not eat in a dignified way?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks how much must be eaten when the eating was not done in a respectable manner.
steps.simpleTranslation: If he did not eat it in a dignified way, what is the law?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא sets up a new question. Until now the small amounts counted because the eating was proper, so now it asks about eating that was not proper.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Small amounts like a cluster of dates work when eaten in a normal, dignified way. If the eating was not dignified, a tiny amount may not be enough, so a larger amount must be set. The next step gives that amount.

phrases.english: If he did not eat it in a dignified way, what is the law?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from dignified eating to eating that was not dignified.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What minimum amount of non-dignified eating counts as 'eating' from the wife's property.

steps.title: An איסר's worth or a דינר's worth
steps.stepSummary: עולא reports that two אמוראים in ארץ ישראל disagree: one says an איסר's worth, the other a דינר's worth.
steps.simpleTranslation: עולא said: two אמוראים in the West disagree about this. One says the value of an איסר, and one says the value of a דינר.
steps.whatsHappening: עולא answers the question by reporting a disagreement. Some value must be eaten, but they argue whether it is an איסר or a דינר.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Since the eating was not dignified, a token amount is not enough, and a money value is set instead. An איסר is a small coin and a דינר is a much larger one, so the two opinions are far apart. Either way, non-dignified eating needs a measurable value.
steps.whatToRemember: Dignified eating counts even in tiny amounts, like a cluster of dates. Non-dignified eating needs at least an איסר's or a דינר's worth.

phrases.english: Ulla said:
Two amoraim in the West disagree about it,
one said: with an issar's worth,
and one said: with a dinar's worth.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר עוּלָּא: פְּלִיגִי בַּהּ תְּרֵי אָמוֹרָאֵי בְּמַעְרְבָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 4.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: There is a dispute: non-dignified eating counts if it is worth an איסר according to one opinion, or a דינר according to the other.

steps.title: רב יהודה's ruling about bundles of vine branches
steps.stepSummary: The judges of פומבדיתא report that רב יהודה ruled in an actual case that using bundles of vine branches from the wife's property counts as eating.
steps.simpleTranslation: The judges of פומבדיתא say: רב יהודה ruled in an actual case about bundles of vine branches.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a real case. The husband used bundles of vine branches from his wife's property, not fruit, and רב יהודה ruled that this counts as 'eating' her property.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Up to now we spoke about eating fruit. This case shows that benefiting from other parts of the property, like branches, also counts. So the husband loses his claim for expenses here too.

keyTerms.meaning: He acted in a real case (gave a practical ruling)

steps.whyThisMatters: It widens 'eating' to include any real benefit from the property, not only eating fruit.

phrases.english: The judges of Pumbedita say:
Rav Yehuda acted in an actual case
with bundles of vine branches.
phrases.notes: The husband took these branches from his wife's property, and רב יהודה counted it as 'eating' from it.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמְרִי דַּיָּינֵי דְּפוּמְבְּדִיתָא: עֲבַד רַב יְהוּדָה עוֹבָדָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds another kind of benefit, branches, that counts as 'eating'.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Benefiting from bundles of vine branches of the wife's property counts as eating, so the husband loses his claim for expenses.

steps.title: רב יהודה is consistent with his view on חזקה
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא shows that this ruling fits רב יהודה's other ruling: eating ערלה, שביעית, or כלאים from a field still counts as a חזקה.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יהודה follows his own reasoning, as רב יהודה said: if he ate ערלה, שביעית, or כלאים, this counts as a חזקה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains that רב יהודה's branches ruling matches another ruling of his about taking ownership of land (חזקה).
steps.deeperAnalysis: Someone working a field of ערלה, שביעית, or כלאים cannot get normal benefit from the fruit. Yet רב יהודה still counts it as a חזקה, because he got other benefit from the field, such as the branches. In the same way, here benefit from branches counts as 'eating' the wife's property.

keyTerms.meaning: Following his own reasoning (consistent with his other ruling)
Fruit of a tree in its first three years, forbidden
Taking ownership of land by using it

steps.confusionAlert: רב יהודה does not mean that the forbidden fruit itself was allowed. The point is that other benefit from the field, like the branches, is enough.

phrases.english: Rav Yehuda follows his own reasoning,
as Rav Yehuda said:
if he ate from it orla, the seventh year, or diverse kinds,
phrases.notes: 'It' is a field someone is trying to claim as his own by using it.

phrases.english: this is a chazaka.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַב יְהוּדָה לְטַעְמֵיהּ, דְּאָמַר רַב יְהוּדָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Grounds רב יהודה's practical ruling in his own broader principle.
steps.raayaObject: רב יהודה's ruling that using vine branches counts as eating the wife's property.
steps.raayaSupportSource: רב יהודה's ruling that eating from a field of ערלה, שביעית, or כלאים still counts as a חזקה, since benefit other than the fruit is enough.

steps.title: Spending on a קטנה wife's property is like spending on a stranger's
steps.stepSummary: רב חסדא rules that a husband who spends on the property of his wife who is a קטנה is treated like someone who spends on another person's property.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יעקב said in the name of רב חסדא: one who spends money on the property of his wife who is a קטנה is like one who spends on someone else's property.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens a new ruling about a special case: a husband married to a קטנה. His spending on her property is treated like a stranger's spending.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A קטנה married through her mother or brothers can leave the marriage through מיאון. In that case the husband is not treated like a regular husband who loses out. Like an outsider who improves another's field, he gets paid back for the improvement.

keyTerms.meaning: Expenses spent on improving the property

steps.whyThisMatters: It is a clear exception to the general rule for husbands. Her status as his wife stays, but the expense rule follows the rule for outsiders.

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַב יַעֲקֹב אָמַר רַב חִסְדָּא:
phrases.english: Rav Yaakov said that Rav Chisda said:

phrases.aramaic: הַמּוֹצִיא הוֹצָאוֹת עַל נִכְסֵי אִשְׁתּוֹ קְטַנָּה —
phrases.english: one who spends expenses on the property of his wife who is a minor,
is like one who spends on someone else's property.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב יַעֲקֹב אָמַר רַב חִסְדָּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Shifts from defining 'eating' to a special case where the husband's expense rule is different.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A husband of a קטנה who spends on her property is treated like an outsider who improves another's property, so if she leaves through מיאון, he is paid back for the improvement.

steps.title: The reason: so he will not let her property decline
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא explains that the חכמים made this תקנה so the husband would not let her property deteriorate.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is the reason? The חכמים made an enactment for her, so that he will not let her property go to ruin.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks for the reason behind רב חסדא's ruling and answers it right away. It is a תקנה to protect the girl's property.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If he knew he might lose his money when she does מיאון, he would not take care of her fields. By promising him repayment like an outsider, the חכמים make sure he keeps her property in good shape.

keyTerms.meaning: He would let them be ruined

steps.whatToRemember: A husband of a קטנה is paid back like an outsider. This is a תקנה of the חכמים so that he will look after her property.

phrases.english: What is the reason?
The Rabbis made an enactment for her,
so that he will not let them go to ruin.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the reason for רב חסדא's ruling in step 8.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The חכמים made a תקנה guaranteeing repayment so that the husband would keep up her property instead of letting it decline.

steps.title: The husband who fetched his wife's inheritance from בי חוזאי
steps.stepSummary: A husband spent 600 of his own זוזים to bring back his wife's 400, used one of hers on the way, and רבי אמי ruled he cannot claim anything.
steps.simpleTranslation: A woman inherited 400 זוזים in בי חוזאי. Her husband spent 600 of his own money to go and bring back the 400. On the way back he needed one זוז and took it from her money. He came to רבי אמי, who said: 'What he spent, he spent, and what he ate, he ate.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tells a real case. רבי אמי applies the משנה's rule 'he spent much and ate a little,' so the husband gets nothing back.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה says that if a husband spent on his wife's property and also benefited from it even a little, he cannot claim his expenses. רבי אמי treats the one זוז the husband took as 'eating.' That means the 600 he spent is lost.

keyTerms.term: מַה שֶּׁהוֹצִיא הוֹצִיא וּמַה שֶּׁאָכַל אָכַל
keyTerms.meaning: What he spent is gone and what he ate is his: no claims either way

phrases.english: There was a certain woman to whom there fell (by inheritance)
four hundred zuz in Bei Chozai.
The husband went and spent six hundred (of his own)
and brought back four hundred.
While he was coming back,
he needed one zuz
and took it from them (her money).
He came before Rabbi Ami.
He said to him: What he spent, he spent,
and what he ate, he ate.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens a new case about a husband's expenses on his wife's property.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבי אמי: taking one זוז counts as 'eating,' so the husband cannot claim his 600.

steps.title: The רבנן object: he used principal, not produce
steps.stepSummary: The רבנן argue that the משנה's 'eating' means eating the produce. Taking from the principal is just counted as part of his expenses.
steps.simpleTranslation: The רבנן said to רבי אמי: That rule applies when he eats the produce. But this man took from the principal itself, and that is just expenses.
steps.whatsHappening: The רבנן challenge רבי אמי's ruling. They say this case does not count as 'he ate.'
steps.deeperAnalysis: A husband has a right to the produce (פירות) of his wife's property, not to the principal (קרן). The one זוז came from the inheritance itself, so it is not his 'eating.' It is just money he took back toward what he spent.

phrases.english: The Rabbis said to Rabbi Ami:
This applies where he eats the produce,
but this one ate the principal,
and that is expenditure.
phrases.notes: He means the זוז is just part of his spending money, as if he paid himself back a little.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges רבי אמי's ruling in step 10.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי אמי's ruling that taking one זוז counts as 'eating.'
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: 'Eating' in the משנה means eating produce. Taking principal is only spending, so the 'ate a little' rule does not apply.

steps.title: רבי אמי agrees: he swears and collects
steps.stepSummary: רבי אמי accepts the point. This is a case of 'spent and did not eat,' so the husband swears how much he spent and collects it.
steps.simpleTranslation: If so, this is a case of 'he spent and did not eat.' He swears how much he spent and takes it.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי אמי accepts the רבנן's objection and changes his ruling. The husband now gets his expenses back with an oath.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Once the זוז is not counted as eating, the case moves into the משנה's other category, 'spent and did not eat.' In that category the husband swears to the amount and is paid back.
steps.whatToRemember: Only using the produce counts as 'eating' that cancels a husband's claim. Taking from the principal does not.

phrases.aramaic: אִם כֵּן, הָוֵה לֵיהּ הוֹצִיא וְלֹא אָכַל,
phrases.english: If so, it is a case of 'he spent and did not eat,'
so he swears how much he spent, and takes it.

steps.triggerLanguage: אִם כֵּן, הָוֵה לֵיהּ הוֹצִיא וְלֹא אָכַל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: רבי אמי accepts the objection of step 11 and revises his ruling.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: The husband swears how much he spent and collects it, because using principal is not 'eating.'

steps.title: רבי אסי limits the oath rule to matching improvement
steps.stepSummary: Quoting the משנה's 'he swears and takes,' רבי אסי adds that this applies only when the improvement to the property matches the expense.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה said: 'He swears how much he spent and takes it.' רבי אסי said: This is only when there is improvement to the property equal to the expense.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא goes back to the משנה's words. רבי אסי adds a condition to them.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The husband does not simply get back whatever he spent. His expense has to be matched by a real improvement (שבח) in the property. It is not yet clear whether this is a strict limit or a leniency; the next step asks exactly that.

phrases.english: 'He swears how much he spent and takes it.'
Rabbi Asi said:
And this is only when there is improvement equal to the expense.

steps.triggerLanguage: יִשָּׁבַע כַּמָּה הוֹצִיא וְיִטּוֹל. אָמַר רַבִּי אַסִּי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Leaves the story and returns to the wording of the משנה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The husband's 'swear and take' applies when the improvement matches the expense.

steps.title: What practical difference does רבי אסי's condition make?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what practical law רבי אסי's condition teaches.
steps.simpleTranslation: For what law (was this said)?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks what רבי אסי's condition changes in practice. This sets up the next two answers.
steps.deeperAnalysis: 'Improvement equal to the expense' could cut either way. It could be a strict rule, that he gets less when the improvement is smaller. Or it could be a leniency, that no oath is needed when the improvement is bigger.

keyTerms.meaning: For what practical law? It asks what difference a statement makes in practice.

phrases.english: For what law?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the practical meaning of רבי אסי's statement.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Is רבי אסי's condition a stringency or a leniency for the husband?

steps.title: אביי: no oath when improvement exceeds expense
steps.stepSummary: אביי explains that if the improvement is more than the expense, the husband takes his expense without an oath.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said: If the improvement was more than the expense, he takes the expense without an oath.
steps.whatsHappening: אביי answers the question. He reads רבי אסי's condition as a leniency.
steps.deeperAnalysis: When the property clearly went up in value by more than he claims, his claim is believable. So, according to אביי, no oath is needed.

phrases.english: Abaye said:

phrases.aramaic: שֶׁאִם הָיָה שֶׁבַח יָתֵר עַל הוֹצָאָה —
phrases.english: That if the improvement was greater than the expense,
he takes the expense without an oath.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר אַבָּיֵי: שֶׁאִם הָיָה שֶׁבַח יָתֵר עַל הוֹצָאָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 14.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: It is a leniency: if the improvement exceeds the expense, no oath is needed.

steps.title: רבא: that would let the husband cheat
steps.stepSummary: רבא objects that אביי's reading invites deception.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said to him: If so, he will come to trick.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא attacks אביי's explanation. It would let the husband dodge the oath dishonestly.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If no oath is needed whenever the improvement is greater, the husband could always claim a sum a little under the improvement. He would then collect without swearing, even if he really spent less.

phrases.english: Rava said to him:
If so, he will come to deceive!
phrases.notes: He could always claim just under the improvement's value and skip the oath.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ רָבָא: אִם כֵּן, אָתֵי לְאִיעָרוֹמֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges אביי's answer in step 15.
steps.kashyaTarget: אביי's reading that no oath is needed when the improvement exceeds the expense.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Dropping the oath lets the husband invent a claim just below the improvement and collect money he never spent.

steps.title: רבא: expense is capped at the improvement, with an oath
steps.stepSummary: רבא reads רבי אסי's condition as a limit. If the expense was more than the improvement, the husband collects only up to the improvement, and only with an oath.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, רבא said: If the expense was more than the improvement, he gets only expenses up to the amount of the improvement, and with an oath.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא replaces אביי's explanation with his own. רבי אסי's condition is a stringency, not a leniency.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Under רבא's reading, the improvement sets the ceiling on what the husband can collect. The oath is always required, so there is no room to cheat.
steps.whatToRemember: Per רבא, a husband gets back his expenses only up to the property's improvement, and always with an oath.
steps.confusionAlert: Do not mix up the two readings. אביי makes רבי אסי's rule easier on the husband, while רבא makes it a limit, and the oath stays in every case.

phrases.english: Rather, Rava said:

phrases.aramaic: שֶׁאִם הָיְתָה הוֹצָאָה יְתֵירָה עַל הַשֶּׁבַח —
phrases.english: That if the expense was greater than the improvement,

phrases.aramaic: אֵין לוֹ אֶלָּא הוֹצָאָה שִׁיעוּר שֶׁבַח, וּבִשְׁבוּעָה.
phrases.english: he has only the expense up to the amount of the improvement, and with an oath.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא אָמַר רָבָא: שֶׁאִם הָיְתָה הוֹצָאָה יְתֵירָה עַל הַשֶּׁבַח
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Offers a new answer to step 14 after rejecting אביי's answer in step 16.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: It is a stringency: expenses are capped at the improvement, and an oath is always required.
steps.whyThisMatters: It sets how much a husband can recover for improving his wife's property, and it keeps the oath so he cannot collect money he never spent.

steps.title: Do the husband's sharecroppers leave when he leaves?
steps.stepSummary: A new question: a husband hired sharecroppers to work his wife's land. If the husband leaves the land, do they leave too, or do they stay?
steps.simpleTranslation: They asked: a husband put sharecroppers on the land in his place. What is the law? Did they come to work because of the husband, so when he leaves they leave? Or did they come to work because of the land, and land is always meant to be worked by sharecroppers?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens a new question, an איבעיא, about sharecroppers a husband hired to work his wife's property. It wants to know what happens to them when the husband leaves the land, for example after a divorce.
steps.deeperAnalysis: There are two ways to see the sharecroppers. Either they are tied to the husband and only stand in his place, so they lose their spot when he leaves. Or they are tied to the land, which always needs sharecroppers no matter who owns it, so they keep their spot.

keyTerms.meaning: A question was raised before the Sages (an open question)
Sharecroppers, who work a field for a share of its crops
With the intention of, because of
Went down to the field, meaning started working it

phrases.english: They asked:
A husband who put sharecroppers in his place, what is the law?
Did he go down to work because of the husband?
Then once the husband leaves, they leave too.
Or perhaps he went down to work because of the land,
and land, as it stands, stands ready for sharecroppers?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens a new question, still about a husband's dealings with his wife's property.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Are sharecroppers hired by the husband tied to the husband, so they leave with him, or tied to the land, so they stay?

steps.title: Even someone who plants without permission gets paid
steps.stepSummary: רבא בר רב חנן challenges the question: someone who plants another person's field without permission still gets paid the smaller amount, so why would these sharecroppers get nothing?
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא בר רב חנן objected: how is this different from someone who went into his friend's field and planted it without permission? We assess what he is owed, and he gets the lower amount.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא בר רב חנן attacks the first side of the question, which says the sharecroppers simply leave. He compares them to a known case where even an unauthorized planter is still paid something.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the case of היורד לתוך שדה חבירו, a man who plants without permission is still paid. He gets either his costs or the value he added, whichever is less. So even if the sharecroppers had no right to be there, they should get at least that, and leaving with nothing seems impossible.

keyTerms.meaning: Objects to it, raises a strong challenge
One who goes into his friend's field and works it
We assess for him how much he is owed
He is at a disadvantage and gets the smaller amount

phrases.aramaic: מַתְקֵיף לַהּ רָבָא בַּר רַב חָנָן:
phrases.english: Rava bar Rav Ḥanan objected to it:

phrases.aramaic: מַאי שְׁנָא מֵהַיּוֹרֵד לְתוֹךְ שְׂדֵה חֲבֵירוֹ
phrases.english: How is this different from one who goes into his friend's field
and plants it without permission,
where we assess for him, and he has the lower hand?
phrases.notes: He gets his expenses or the value he added to the field, whichever is less.

steps.triggerLanguage: מַתְקֵיף לַהּ רָבָא בַּר רַב חָנָן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the side of the question that says the sharecroppers leave with nothing.
steps.kashyaTarget: The possibility that the sharecroppers leave with the husband and get nothing for their work.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Even an unauthorized planter is paid the smaller amount. So sharecroppers cannot be worse off and leave with nothing.

steps.title: Here the husband would have done the work himself
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers: with the unauthorized planter, no one else would have worked the field. Here, the husband would have worked it.
steps.simpleTranslation: There, there is no one who would make the effort. Here, there is the husband, who makes the effort.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא defends the question by showing that the two cases are not the same.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The unauthorized planter gets paid because the field would otherwise have sat unworked, so his work truly helped the owner. Here, the husband was there to do the work. The sharecroppers only took his place, so once he leaves they have no claim of their own.

keyTerms.meaning: Makes the effort, takes the trouble

phrases.english: There, there is no person who makes the effort,
here, there is the husband, who makes the effort.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers רבא בר רב חנן's objection by showing the comparison does not hold.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The sharecroppers should be paid like any unauthorized planter.
steps.terutzMaskana: The planter is paid because no one else would have worked the field. The sharecroppers only replace the husband, who would have worked it himself.

steps.title: What is the final ruling?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what the conclusion is on the original question.
steps.simpleTranslation: What was decided about it?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks for the final answer to the question about the sharecroppers. This line sets up the ruling that comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The back-and-forth showed that both sides of the question make sense. So the גמרא now asks for a practical decision.

phrases.english: What was concluded about it?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Goes back to the original question from step 18 and asks for a final ruling.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The final law about sharecroppers once the husband leaves.

steps.title: It depends on whether the husband is a sharecropper himself
steps.stepSummary: רב הונא בריה דרב יהושע rules: if the husband knows how to farm, the workers only replaced him and leave with him. If he does not, the land needed sharecroppers anyway, so they stay.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב הונא, son of רב יהושע, said: we look at the case. If the husband is a sharecropper himself, then when the husband leaves, they leave. If the husband is not a sharecropper, the land stands ready for sharecroppers.
steps.whatsHappening: רב הונא בריה דרב יהושע gives the final ruling. It depends on whether the husband could have farmed the land himself.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This ruling uses both sides of the original question. If the husband could farm, the workers just took his place, as step 20 said, so they leave with him. If he could not farm, the land needed sharecroppers no matter who owned it, so they are tied to the land and stay.

keyTerms.meaning: We look and examine the situation
A sharecropper, someone who knows how to work fields

steps.whatToRemember: Sharecroppers leave with the husband only if he could have worked the land himself. If he could not, the land needed sharecroppers anyway, so they keep their place.

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַב הוּנָא בְּרֵיהּ דְּרַב יְהוֹשֻׁעַ:
phrases.english: Rav Huna, son of Rav Yehoshua, said:
We look: if the husband is a sharecropper himself,
phrases.notes: He means the husband knows how to farm and would have done the work himself.

phrases.english: once the husband leaves, they leave.
If the husband is not a sharecropper,
the land stands ready for sharecroppers.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב הוּנָא בְּרֵיהּ דְּרַב יְהוֹשֻׁעַ: חָזֵינַן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 21 and settles the question of step 18.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: It depends on whether the husband is himself a sharecropper.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: If the husband could farm, the sharecroppers leave with him. If not, they stay with the land.

steps.title: Can the husband sell the produce of his wife's land?
steps.stepSummary: An איבעיא: if a בעל sells his wife's land for its produce, is the sale valid? Either he can sell what he owns, or the רבנן's rule giving him the produce has a limited purpose.
steps.simpleTranslation: A question was asked: A husband sold his wife's land for its produce. What is the law? Do we say that whatever he owns, he can pass on to someone else? Or perhaps, when the רבנן set up that the produce goes to the husband... (the sentence continues).
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens a new question (an איבעיא) about whether a husband can sell his right to the produce of his wife's land. It gives the first side fully and only starts the second side, which continues next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The husband owns the produce, so the simple idea is that an owner can sell what is his. The other side looks at why the רבנן gave him the produce at all. If they gave it for a certain purpose, maybe he cannot hand it to a stranger. The question is whether his right is full ownership or a right tied to the reason it was given.

keyTerms.meaning: A question was asked of them. It opens an unresolved question in the בית מדרש.
Land for its produce. He sells the right to the crops, not the land itself.
What he owns, he can transfer. An owner can pass on what is his.
Or perhaps. This introduces the second side of the question.

steps.confusionAlert: The husband is not selling his wife's land itself. He is selling only his right to the crops that grow on it.

phrases.english: A question was asked of them:
A husband who sold his wife's land for its produce, what is the law?
phrases.notes: He sold the right to eat the crops. The land still belongs to his wife.

phrases.english: Do we say
that whatever he owns, he has transferred,
phrases.notes: Some versions don't have the word in round brackets. The meaning is the same either way.

phrases.english: or perhaps:
when the רבנן set it up for him
that the produce goes to the husband...

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from the sharecroppers the husband hired (steps 18-22) to a new question: can the husband sell his right to the produce outright?
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Is a husband's sale of the produce rights of his wife's land valid? It depends on whether he owns the produce fully, or whether the רבנן gave it to him for a purpose that blocks selling it.
